description: DAW Pro's own drum machine (m39-dm), eight synthesised voices, playing ONE 4-bar groove at 120 BPM. The single axis is the KIT: every variant plays a byte-identical pattern and differs only in which factory preset is loaded. 808 is the control AND the instrument's defaults. The open hat on the 'and of 4' is choked by the next downbeat's closed hat in EVERY variant — that is constant, not the axis, but it is audible and worth pointing at.

variants.axis: preset = 808 — THE CONTROL, and also the instrument's DEFAULTS (DrumKitParams.presets[0].params == DrumKitParams(), verified in source): long sub kick with a slow fall, loose hats, a snare that sits back. This is what a track sounds like the moment you pick Drum Machine.
preset = 909 — the OTHER lineage. Same topology, different numbers: a faster and deeper pitch sweep on the kick, a much shorter kick body, a brighter snappier snare, tighter hats.

variants.name: acoustic
variants.axis: preset = acoustic — drive removed everywhere, inharmonic snare modes, longer tails and a wider stereo image (hats, cymbal and tom panned apart). The least synthetic of the five.

variants.name: lofi
variants.axis: preset = lofi — dull and driven. Every voice darker (tone pulled down), the kick and snare saturated, the hats short and closed down.

variants.name: trap
variants.axis: preset = trap — a very long sub kick, a clap-forward snare and fast bright hats built for rolls. MEASURED SEPARATELY: most of its distance from the control lives below 200 Hz, which a laptop speaker cannot reproduce — see the report's per-band numbers.
